brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: Portable electronics organizer: a base to hold the parts
requirements.evidence: Hex base · Full piece at (0,0,0) plus a Hex base · North half at (0,-1,0) forming a compact two-block base.
Bin, full depth, 3 compartments (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3) drops into the full cell at (0,0,0) and hangs on its rim, so it can be lifted out. Mesh check clear.
Drawer drawer:0#0,-1#cut (classic style, key s) mounted on the cut face of the North half base at (0,-1,0).
Handle handle:0,0,0;top sits on the top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) of the full base, with its inserts. Mesh check reports clear.

finish.summary: Built a two-block portable organizer: a full hex base with a removable 3-compartment bin, a top cover carrying a carry handle, and a drawer on the North half base. check_build reports meshClash "clear" with no rule errors (only informational open-cap notices). This checks fit only; no strength or load claims are made. Sizing and any electronics-specific needs (e.g., ESD material) were not addressed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
